intro: Wet rooms are one of the most practical and stylish bathroom upgrades you can make, and demand for them in Roslin has grown steadily as homeowners look to modernise ageing bathrooms or create accessible spaces for older family members. The appeal is obvious — a fully waterproofed, level-access shower area is easier to clean, safer underfoot, and adds genuine value to a property. But getting one installed properly takes more than ripping out a bath and laying some tiles. In Roslin, the specific challenges of the local housing stock mean that wet room installation needs careful planning, the right waterproofing system, and a tradesperson who understands what they're working with before a single tile goes up.
localContext: Roslin's housing mix is genuinely varied, and that variation matters enormously when planning a wet room. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up much of the town's character come with walls that can be uneven, floors that aren't always level, and subfloors that may be timber rather than solid concrete — all of which affect how a wet room is designed and waterproofed. Timber subfloors, in particular, require a different tanking approach compared to solid floors, and they need careful assessment before any work begins to ensure there's no existing moisture ingress or rot that would undermine the installation. Roslin's newer modern estates present fewer structural surprises, but even here, getting the drainage fall right and ensuring adequate ventilation is essential. As a moderately hard water area, Roslin homeowners should also be aware that limescale can build up on fixtures and screens over time — so opting for quality fittings with hard water resistance and keeping on top of regular descaling will help your wet room look its best for longer.
serviceDetail: A professional wet room installation in Roslin typically follows a clear sequence, though the timeline and specifics will vary depending on your property type and the scope of the project. The process starts with a site survey, where the installer assesses the existing bathroom, checks the subfloor construction, looks at drainage options, and discusses your design preferences. For older Roslin properties especially, this survey stage isn't just a formality — it often reveals things like inadequate existing drainage falls or damp that need addressing before any new work begins. Once the design and specification are agreed, the existing bathroom fittings are stripped out and the subfloor is prepared. If you have a timber floor, a suitable deck is laid to create a stable, rigid base. The waterproofing system — typically a tanking membrane applied to walls and floor — is then installed, and this is arguably the most critical stage. A wet room is only as good as its waterproofing, and any shortcuts here will cause costly problems down the line. Drainage channels or floor drains are set in with the correct gradient to ensure water flows away effectively. Tiling or other wall and floor finishes are applied next, followed by fitting your chosen shower fixtures, screens if required, and any additional features like underfloor heating, which many Roslin homeowners add at this stage. Final checks, sealing, and a full test of the drainage and fixtures complete the job.
pricing: In Roslin, a wet room installation typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000, with most projects falling somewhere in the middle of that range. The key factors that push costs up are the condition of the existing subfloor (timber floors requiring additional preparation cost more than solid concrete), the size of the space, the quality of tiles and fixtures chosen, and any associated work like moving soil pipes or upgrading ventilation. Period cottages in Roslin often sit at the higher end due to the preparatory work involved. Adding underfloor heating will typically add £500–£1,200 depending on the floor area. Always get a detailed written quote that breaks out materials and labour separately.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Roslin and the surrounding Midlothian area makes a real difference with a job like this. A local installer will have worked in similar stone-built properties and cottages before — they'll know the quirks, they'll have reliable local suppliers, and they won't be quoting blind on access or logistics. They're also easier to hold accountable if any snagging issues arise after the job is done. Word of mouth matters in a smaller community like Roslin, and tradespeople who work locally tend to take pride in the quality of their work for exactly that reason.

faqs.q: Is my older Roslin stone-built cottage suitable for a wet room?
faqs.a: Most older properties in Roslin can accommodate a wet room, but they do require more preparation than modern builds. Timber subfloors need to be properly boarded and the waterproofing system selected accordingly. A thorough survey before any work starts is essential — a good installer will identify and solve these challenges rather than paper over them.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Roslin?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Roslin take between five and ten working days, depending on the size of the room, the condition of the existing bathroom, and whether any remedial structural work is needed first. Older properties sometimes require a few extra days if damp or drainage issues are found during the strip-out phase.

faqs.q: Will limescale be a problem in my Roslin wet room?
faqs.a: Roslin sits in a moderately hard water area, so some limescale build-up on shower heads, drains, and glass screens is likely over time. Choosing fixtures rated for hard water and using a regular descaling spray will keep things looking clean. Some homeowners also fit an inline shower head filter to reduce scale build-up on fittings.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Roslin?
faqs.a: In most cases, no — wet room installation is classed as permitted development and doesn't require planning permission. However, if your Roslin property is listed or in a designated area, it's worth checking with Midlothian Council before starting work. Your installer should be able to advise on this during the initial survey.
